comments.content: - **`src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.cpp:1503`** — All three new definitions (lines 1503, 1514, and 1524) take only `std::string`, but their declarations take `App::DocumentObject*` plus `std::string`. Building TechDraw therefore fails with “no declaration matches” errors for these methods.

**1. `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.cpp` lines 1502, 1513, 1523 vs `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.h` lines 243–245 — declaration/definition mismatch, the module cannot compile.**
The header adds `static bool isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);` (and siblings), but the definitions at 1502/1513/1523 are non-static, take only `std::string element`, and call the non-static members `getProjVertexByIndex` / `getEdge` unqualified.
Failure scenario: building the TechDraw App target. Every compiler rejects the definitions with "no declaration matches 'bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string)'". And neither possible repair direction is consistent: if the signatures are "fixed" to the static two-arg form, the bodies still cannot call `getEdge()`/`getProjVertexByIndex()` without an instance (static member → "cannot call member function without object"); if instead the declarations were made non-static one-arg, then any caller updated to the new API breaks the other way. As committed, no caller, signature, or calling convention makes this TU compile.

**2. `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawUtil.cpp` (removed lines, old 1855–1890) and `DrawUtil.h` (removed lines, old 249–254) — public API deleted without any in-diff migration of callers, and the replacement's two-arg static form is never defined.**
The old `DrawUtil::isCosmeticVertex(owner, element)` etc. were the only API that existed for this query; the diff removes them and shows zero call-site updates, while the newly *declared* `DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject*, std::string)` at `DrawViewPart.h:243` exists only as a declaration — it is never defined (see item 1). Failure scenario: any existing caller of `DrawUtil::isCosmeticVertex(owner, element)` — none of which this diff touches — fails with "isCosmeticVertex is not a member of DrawUtil"; and a caller migrated to `DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(owner, element)` compiles only if it resolves the name, then fails at link time with an undefined reference, since the declared static function has no definition. Given the old functions were `TechDrawExport` public API, external callers are expected; the diff provides no migration for them.**DEFECT 1: Header/implementation signature mismatch in `DrawViewPart`**

**File:** `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.h` (lines 242-244) vs `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.cpp` (lines 1501, 1513, 1525)

The header declares three **static** methods taking two parameters:
```cpp
static bool isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
static bool isCosmeticEdge(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
static bool isCenterLine(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
```

But the `.cpp` defines them as **non-static member functions** taking only one parameter:
```cpp
bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string element)  // no 'static', no owner
bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticEdge(std::string element)
bool DrawViewPart::isCenterLine(std::string element)
```

**Failure scenario:** Any translation unit including `DrawViewPart.h` and calling `DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(obj, "Vertex1")` will fail to link — the declared symbol expects two arguments and static linkage, while the definition is a non-static member function with one argument (implicit `this`). Build breaks.

---

**DEFECT 2: Lost `owner` parameter breaks call sites**

**File:** `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.cpp` (lines 1501, 1513, 1525)

The original `DrawUtil` versions accepted an `owner` (cast to `DrawViewPart*`) and operated on it. The new member-function versions operate on `this`. Callers that pass a *different* `DrawViewPart` instance as `owner` will now incorrectly operate on the wrong object (the callee's `this`).

**Failure scenario:** Code elsewhere calls `DrawViewPart::isCosmeticEdge(someOtherView, "Edge1")` — after this change, it compiles (if header matched) but reads edges from `this` instead of `someOtherView`, returning wrong cosmetic/centerline status for the target view.
